trust_decision.summary: Dozzle's label filter (per-user user.ContainerLabels, else the global --filter) is what decides which containers a caller may observe; at the pinned commit it is applied on the list/find paths but not on the GET /api/events/stream consumer, which forwards every container's stat, lifecycle, update and health payloads regardless of the caller's labels.

landing_point.why: The summary names the statistics stream, so the stat case is the first place an engineer looks; the same handler then forwards the unfiltered lifecycle, update and health branches at :68-108.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/events/stream (container-event channel, plus the containers-changed refresh on start/rename)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: MCP is an opt-in, server-wide integration (--enable-mcp defaults to false, docs/guide/mcp.md:12) whose documented job is to list all containers across all hosts (docs/guide/mcp.md:40), so a solver can argue per-user label filters were never part of that surface.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Stats for containers the caller may see must keep flowing even though a ContainerStat carries only an ID and metrics and no Host field; an over-broad fix that gates stats on the event's host map drops the whole container-stat channel, which is why the published fix needs an empty-host fallback that scans every host (fix.diff:92-99). The initial containers-changed payload for visible containers must likewise still be emitted.

O6_input_shapes: stat payload with no host field (only id plus cpu/memory/network/disk numbers), so identity must be matched by ID across all hosts
lifecycle event carrying host and actorId (start, die, destroy, rename, pause, unpause), where both fields must agree
update event carrying a full *container.Container that may be nil
health_status event whose identity lives only in actorId while the payload is built locally
per-host containers-changed refresh list produced by ListContainersForHost with the caller's labels, which must also refresh the visible set
multi-host fan-in: the same container ID can exist on two hosts, so an ID-only fallback has to scan every host

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/mcp: the MCP tools list_containers (internal/mcp/server.go:105) and get_container_stats (internal/mcp/server.go:324-358) call the host service with the server-wide h.config.Labels handed in at internal/web/routes.go:222 and never with the caller's ContainerLabels, so a label-restricted authenticated user can enumerate other containers and read their stats history.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: MCP is disabled by default, is described as a server-wide 'list all containers across all hosts' integration, and its docs never mention filters, so it looks like a separate surface rather than a user view.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: internal/web/events.go -> internal/web/routes.go:221-224 wiring -> internal/mcp/server.go, a separate package (2 files, 1 package boundary)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/notifications/preview: previewExpression matches containers fetched with container.ContainerLabels{} (no user filter) and returns matchedContainers (full container.Container including its stats ring buffer, internal/container/types.go:28) plus matchedLogs to any authenticated caller.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Notification rules are an authoring/test surface for administrators rather than a container view; the endpoint only exists to preview expressions.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package internal/web, 3 files from the landing point (registered at internal/web/routes.go:205)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/debug/store: debugStore lists every container on every host with container.ContainerLabels{} and returns them as JSON, bypassing both the global filter and the caller's labels.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Debug-only route, mounted only when debug logging is enabled at startup (internal/web/routes.go:186-188), so it reads as a diagnostic tool, not a user surface.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package internal/web, 2 files from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A sixth channel added to the same select (e.g. container-mount or an update-progress event) that forwards a Container or an ID payload without consulting the visible set.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already forwards five differently shaped channels and the frontend subscribes to each named event (assets/stores/container.ts:58-67); new stream events are added there feature by feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new MCP tool (get_container_events, stream_stats, search_logs) registered with the same s.labels field.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: All four existing tools pass s.labels and tools are added one at a time; nothing in tool registration can see the requesting user.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new log or stat stream route whose per-container filter closure is built from h.config.Labels instead of h.resolveLabels(r).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: streamHostLogs and streamHostGroupLogs already build ad-hoc filter closures passed to streamLogsForContainers; copying one and using h.config.Labels compiles and looks right.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another preview or diagnostic endpoint that lists containers with an empty ContainerLabels to show what a rule would match.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Preview code needs containers regardless of who is asking, and the empty-filter idiom already appears twice in the tree (internal/web/notifications.go:572, internal/web/debug.go:13).

O9_family: authorization / information exposure (CWE-285 improper authorization, CWE-200 exposure of container telemetry)

O10_build.toolchain: go + make; `make test` runs fake_assets and generate (openssl certs, protoc for pb regeneration) then `go test -cover -race -count 1 -timeout 40s ./...`; pnpm is only needed for the real dist build, fake_assets stubs dist/index.html
O10_build.project_tests: internal/web/events_test.go drives CreateServer with a mocked Docker client (routes_test.go MockedClient) and asserts abide snapshots in internal/web/__snapshots__/web.snapshot; internal/mcp/server_test.go exercises the MCP host service. No Docker daemon, GPU or network needed for the events/stream tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Filter only the container-event payload against a per-request ListContainersForHost set and key everything by the event's host, which leaves container-stat, container-updated and container-health open and silently drops every stat because ContainerStat carries no host.

out_of_scope_notes: internal/docker/stats_collector.go:104,131: the collector lists with its own labels but starts a stats stream for any 'start' event without re-checking them, so unfiltered stats are produced upstream of the web layer (recorded as the sink's producer, not pursued as a separate user route).

internal/web/download.go:31-35 dereferences auth.UserFromContext output without a nil check inside the authenticated group; a possible nil-pointer panic under simple auth, unrelated to this advisory, not pursued.

internal/agent/server.go:82,105,132 resolve containers with an empty ContainerLabels on the agent gRPC port; that port is a trusted internal boundary and the main instance resolves visibility before the call, so it was not pursued.
